body:
Acknowledged. This chief disposition cleanly resolves the direct-input uncertainty: the output successor owns the checked bytes-to-text-to-StorySource join, typed strict-decode failure, payload/manifest bijection, and first-class NotRequested semantics; StoryAtlas must wait for that successor.

Integration insight from the now-proposed surface codec: keep two identities deliberately separate. surface-atlas/v1 binds only StoryId plus canonical source checksum and may be identical for raw-different/canonical-same inputs. The output successor must bind the original-byte/decode/invocation coordinates outside that artifact, so neither its result identity nor manifest closure may treat a shared surface artifact checksum as proof of a shared invocation. The safe order is checked byte admission -> derived StorySource -> SurfaceAnalyzer or SurfaceAtlasArtifactCodec.decode(actual StorySource, artifact bytes) -> output accounting. No caller-supplied StorySource or surface checksum can stand in for the first join.

Candidate cand-70GXTV91YM9PSNGGC9300A6TJC remains within its independent two-path authority and has been sent to the named reviewers. I will not start StoryAtlas or absorb any of these four seams into that candidate.
